extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers and practitioners interested in public health, sanitary practice, and methods for clarifying scientific ideas (readers of Popular Science Monthly; physicians, public-health officers, students of logic)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and standards for making ideas clear and distinct in scientific reasoning (methods of thought: doubt, definition, and practical consequences). Also observational public-health/sanitary practices described as criteria for preventing disease. Useful for authors, teachers, and practitioners aiming to improve reasoning or sanitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privy separation and ventilation
rubrics_metrics.description: A close sliding-door always separates this apartment from the living-room, and a grated window without glass permits thorough ventilation; in country villages the privy stands alongside the road, separate from the house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privies should be physically separated from living areas and ventilated to avoid contamination and discomfort; avoid attaching privies directly to living buildings when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sewage removal frequency and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The important point to be noted ... is in regard to the disposition of their offal, and it is well known that every day or two this is removed and scattered on their rice-fields and other cultivated areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent removal (daily or every two days) of human refuse prevents accumulation, reduces soil saturation, and limits the development of filth-diseases; collected sewage can be used as fertilizer if handled promptly and properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water-tight limited-capacity vaults
rubrics_metrics.description: The vaults consist of water-tight vessels of limited capacity. In Tokio they use for this purpose oil-barrels, which they coat with a kind of varnish inside and out. From the small size of this vessel accumulation never occurs, and from its nature the soil never becomes saturated by its contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use small, water‑tight holding vessels for excreta so they do not accumulate or saturate surrounding soil; small size encourages frequent emptying and reduces environmental contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situate wells away from contamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Their wells are not always properly situated, and the water is liable to pollution from gutters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells and water supplies must be properly located and protected from run-off and gutter contamination to prevent waterborne disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and protection of urban scavengers
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr. David Murray has called my attention to the very important service performed by the crows and a kind of hawk which act as scavengers ... In Japan such a thing is unknown, and the result is that all carrion and other stuff left in the streets are pounced upon and carried off immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing/encouraging natural scavengers (and avoiding their molestation) can aid rapid removal of carrion and refuse from streets and reduce decay-related contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiling drinking water
rubrics_metrics.description: They drink very little cold water. The water is drunk as hot tea — in other words, it is boiled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly boil drinking water (consume as hot tea) to reduce risk of waterborne infections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prolonged maternal breastfeeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Until they are two or three years old, they draw their nourishment from the maternal fount. No child is fed artificially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusive/prolonged breastfeeding in early years is indicated as important in reducing children's disorders and improving child health outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vaccination program and compulsory vaccination
rubrics_metrics.description: Small-pox ... is now coming under control by the Government taking active measures to insure vaccination. A vaccine farm is maintained, and it is compulsory on every one to be vaccinated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain vaccine supply infrastructure (vaccine farms) and implement compulsory or broad vaccination programs to control endemic infectious diseases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve domestic lighting to protect vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Weakness of vision must in some measure be attributed to the poor light the people provide themselves with. A dim candle ... is the almost universal lamp of the Japanese ... The gradual introduction of kerosene-oil, which is now going on, must in some way modify these troubles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide better illumination (improve household lighting, e.g., kerosene or better lamps) to reduce eye strain and near-sightedness associated with dim reading/sewing conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hygienic shaving practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The universal use of the razor in shaving, and the custom of itinerant barbers, who travel from one village to another shaving indiscriminately, indicate too plainly the reason for the prevalence of contagious diseases of the skin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid shared or indiscriminate barbering practices; ensure hygienic shaving instruments and practices to prevent spread of contagious skin diseases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperate habits reduce sunstroke risk
rubrics_metrics.description: It is admitted that intemperance in food or drink, and particularly the latter, may be inducing causes ... it is suggestive to note the rare occurrence of sunstroke among the Japanese ... for a more temperate and frugal people do not exist on the face of the globe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temperate diet and abstention from excessive alcohol and overeating are protective against heat-related illnesses such as sunstroke; behavioral factors may matter more than mere head covering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple building design and safe staging to prevent accidents
rubrics_metrics.description: One observes ... the almost entire absence of deformities arising from accidents — no broken backs or broken noses ... The houses are one story high; generally speaking, there are no windows to tumble out of, or flights of stairs to tumble down ... Their stagings are always built to hold together, and thus pagan temples are reared ... without those appalling accidents which occur ... at home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design dwellings and construction staging to minimize fall risks (one-story houses, secure staging) and limit large factories/unsafe scaffolding to reduce accident-related deformities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider unintended disease-promoting effects of customs
rubrics_metrics.description: As I am mailing this, the alarming news comes that the Asiatic cholera has made its appearance ... curiously enough, the very customs of the people which tend to thwart the ravages of certain other diseases will in this case be the very conditions to promote the ravages of cholera.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how existing cultural/sanitary customs that reduce some disease risks may unintentionally increase risk for others (e.g., cholera); public-health measures must account for disease-specific transmission modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a 'clear' idea
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear idea is defined as one which is so apprehended that it will be recognized wherever it is met with, and so that no other will be mistaken for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for ideas that can be consistently recognized in different contexts; avoid vagueness that prevents reliable identification of the concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a 'distinct' idea
rubrics_metrics.description: A distinct idea is defined as one which contains nothing which is not clear. By the contents of an idea logicians understand whatever is contained in its definition. So that an idea is distinctly apprehended, according to them, when we can give a precise definition of it, in abstract terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise abstract definitions that leave no unclear components; distinctness is the ability to list exactly what belongs to the idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step foundation for clearness: familiarity then definition
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be acknowledged ... that the books are right in making familiarity with a notion the first step toward clearness of apprehension, and the defining of it the second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First become familiar with a notion through use; second, articulate a clear definition. These are necessary initial steps toward clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use doubt to stimulate thought toward belief
rubrics_metrics.description: The action of thought is excited by the irritation of doubt, and ceases when belief is attained ... the production of belief is the sole function of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate appropriate doubts (real or feigned) to trigger inquiry; treat thinking as a process whose goal is to resolve doubt and produce a belief that can guide action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure meaning by habits of action
rubrics_metrics.description: To develop its meaning, we have, therefore, simply to determine what habits it produces, for what a thing means is simply what habits it involves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify ideas by determining the practical consequences and the rules of action they imply; meaning is operationalized via habits or dispositions to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish ideas by possible differences in practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The identity of a habit depends on how it might lead us to act, not merely under such circumstances as are likely to arise, but under such as might possibly occur, no matter how improbable they may be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deciding whether two expressions denote the same idea, examine whether they would lead to different actions under any possible circumstances; practical divergence marks conceptual difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against subjective unclearness and grammatical confusions
rubrics_metrics.description: One singular deception ... is to mistake the sensation produced by our own unclearness of thought for a character of the object we are thinking. Another such deception is to mistake a mere difference in the grammatical construction of two words for a distinction between the ideas they express.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test whether perceived obscurity is due to the thinker (subjective) and whether differences are merely grammatical; seek to reformulate or test ideas so that subjective sensations and grammar do not masquerade as conceptual differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize temporal/structural aspects of thought vs sensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some elements (the sensations) are completely present at every instant so long as they last, while others (like thought) are actions having beginning, middle, and end, and consist in a congruence in the succession of sensations which flow through the mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for the fact that thought involves relations across time (a 'thread' of succession) rather than instantaneous sensations; clarity requires attending to the temporal structure of ideas and their unfolding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belief as a practical stopping/starting place
rubrics_metrics.description: Belief ... appeases the irritation of doubt, and involves the establishment in our nature of a rule of action, or, say for short, a habit. As it appeases the irritation of doubt ... thought relaxes, and comes to rest for a moment when belief is reached. But ... it is also a new starting-place for thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ideas by whether acceptance produces clear rules for action (habits); recognize that accepting a belief both resolves doubt and sets new problems for further inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid perversion of thought (intellectual play that resists resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Among dilettanti ... it is not rare to find those who have so perverted thought to the purposes of pleasure that it seems to vex them to think that the questions upon which they delight to exercise it may ever get finally settled. This disposition is the very debauchery of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for inquiry that seeks resolution rather than perpetual intellectual play; avoid valuing unresolved debate for its own sake when clarity and belief should be the goal.
